# gezor_schema_subject (Resource)

A subject in the cluster's schema registry (Data Schemas). Changing `schema` registers a new version. Applied by the cluster operator, so the cluster must be online.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "gezor_schema_subject" "orders_value" {
  cluster_id    = gezor_cluster.prod.id
  subject       = "orders-value"
  compatibility = "BACKWARD"
  schema = jsonencode({
    type = "record"
    name = "Order"
    fields = [
      { name = "id", type = "string" },
      { name = "total", type = "double" },
    ]
  })

  depends_on = [gezor_cluster_app.schemas]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster id.
- `schema` (String) Schema text. For Avro and JSON Schema, `jsonencode(...)` works well.
- `subject` (String) Subject name, for example `orders-value`.

### Optional

- `compatibility` (String) Subject compatibility, for example `BACKWARD` or `FULL_TRANSITIVE`. Defaults to the registry setting.
- `permanent_delete` (Boolean) Hard-delete every version on destroy instead of a soft delete.
- `schema_type` (String) `AVRO`, `JSON` or `PROTOBUF`.
- `workspace` (String) Workspace id or slug. Defaults to the provider's `workspace`. Changing it recreates the resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<cluster_id>/<subject>`.
- `schema_id` (Number) Registry id of the latest schema.
- `version` (Number) Latest version number.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Append @<workspace> to import from a workspace other than the provider default.
terraform import gezor_schema_subject.example <cluster_id>/<subject>
```
